items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: And there was an arranger named Ron Collier, one of Canada’s most famous arrangers, one of the only guys that ever arranged for Duke Ellington and write for Duke Ellington in Canada. He started this program at Humber...

ctx.x: Did your, your entrance into jazz education and academia, was that partly to change a lifestyle of being on the road?

I never thought I’d be — my father was a music teacher. I helped my music teacher in the school teach younger kids clarinet, never thought about teaching. Went to Potsdam State © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

Teacher’s College and never thought about teaching. Went to Berklee, it never crossed my mind. I moved to Canada in ’74 and I was with Yamaha at the time. I had signed with Yamaha in the States, the last couple of months with Buddy Rich and so when I came to Canada I was with Yamaha. And they called me and they said we’ve got this young student who is, they called him the “rising star” the Yamaha Rising Star Award. And we wondered if you’d give him a couple of lessons. I said gee, I never taught anybody. I don’t…
